findings.reason: the section must extend imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py (or fold its three routines into the generalisation) and its census must name all three claim families, otherwise the generalisation is a parallel copy that drifts from the live `discovery/static` caller.
findings.text: §7 generalises the mapping claim helpers into imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py and states "the module … already holds the claim pattern twice … does not add a third copy", but that is a partial census and a duplicate owner: the SignalSource claim family already lives in the same package at imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py:92 (`claim_signal_sources`), :246 (`release_source_claims`) and :273 (`has_pending_sources`), self-described as "the shared signal sourcing layer" and called live by imas_codex/discovery/static/workers.py:348,415, with a third copy at imas_codex/discovery/mdsplus/graph_ops.py:703 (`claim_signal_sources`), :838 (`release_signal_source_claims`) and :855 (`has_pending_signal_source_work`) — all three use the same `ORDER BY rand()` two-step token pattern over `SignalSource`, so the section adds a fourth home rather than extending the existing owner, and the replacement targets the wrong file (workers.py does not own SignalSource claiming; grouping.py does)

response_events.reason: Partly acted: §7 now names all three SignalSource claim families. The two in grouping.py and mdsplus/graph_ops.py serve the enrichment stage on claimed_at, with live callers in discovery/static; converging them is a separate change, not this plan's product. The generic routine lives in claims.py, the label-agnostic owner used by 24 modules, and is parameterised so they can adopt it.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py hides retrieval, Jev judgment and threshold routing behind `retrieve_candidates`/`route_ids`/`judge_candidates`/`route`, one module owning the candidate stage; §7 routes that stage through the shared `run_discovery_engine` rather than a parallel engine.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 adds the generalised claim/release/pending routines to imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py and records the SignalSource claim pattern as held "twice", but a SignalSource claim family already has a shared home in the same package, and the census is incomplete.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each surface-adding section accounts for itself in its own text: §4 moves the hit build and deletes the `ClusterSearcher` load, §5 states why nothing in these families can retire, §6 names the `mapping_target_*` fields the edge displaces, §7 names the 7→3 helper merge and the two `imas map run` option retirements, §8 names the retired options and fields.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the modules it would extend and cites the mechanism each section reuses (`hybrid_dd_search` imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:97 confirmed as the sync vector owner taking `ids_filter` and `embedding`; `SearchHit` imas_codex/search/search_strategy.py:93 confirmed to carry path/ids_name/documentation/units/data_type/physics_domain/score; `call_decisions`/`acall_decisions` imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3429,3493 confirmed to exist; `run_discovery_engine` imas_codex/discovery/base/engine.py:92 and `OrphanRecoverySpec` imas_codex/discovery/base/supervision.py:875 confirmed; `fetch_cross_facility_mappings`, `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:30, `MODEL_SECTIONS` imas_codex/settings.py:141 all confirmed). The one mechanism it proposes to extend but does not cite is the existing SignalSource claim family, reported under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — both new layers are justified in their own text: §4's `retrieve_candidates` adds batch embedding, cross-IDS score merge, path dedup and a `Candidate` wrapper over `hybrid_dd_search` (the raw hit carries none of those), and §5's judgment calls the shared `call_decisions` layer and states it "builds no second client".
